wildcard_patterns.name: protobuf_ineligible_bare
wildcard_patterns.description: PRIMARY (cross-platform, version-agnostic): renames every bare 'ineligible' literal to same-length 'inexigible'. This subsumes protobuf_name_ineligible and account_ineligible, and additionally rewrites the serialized protobuf descriptor occurrences so descriptor and Go struct tags stay consistent. Because the rename is case-sensitive, Go type/field identifiers (IneligibleTier, IneligibleInfo) are untouched - only the wire/JSON field names change, so protojson no longer binds the server's 'ineligible' key and the eligibility gate sees an unset field. agy 1.2.7: 9 occurrences.

wildcard_patterns.name: protobuf_name_ineligible
wildcard_patterns.description: SUPERSEDED by protobuf_ineligible_bare (kept for older builds): PRIMARY (cross-platform): Renames protobuf field descriptor name=ineligible to name=inexigible (same length). The client no longer sees the field it gates on. Works on all platforms because it targets a string literal, not machine code.

wildcard_patterns.name: account_ineligible
wildcard_patterns.description: SUPERSEDED by protobuf_ineligible_bare (kept for older builds): Cross-platform: Renames 'Account ineligible' string to 'Account inexigible' (same length).

wildcard_patterns.name: not_eligible_region_out_of_scope
wildcard_patterns.description: OPT-IN (off by default, --include-optional): renames a protobuf ENUM VALUE name. Unproven - the eligibility gate is already cleared by protobuf_ineligible_bare, and rewriting an enum name risks a parse mismatch if the server sends the enum by name rather than by number. Left in the registry for experiments, not applied by default. Cross-platform: Rewrites NOT_ELIGIBLE_REGION_OUT_OF_SCOPE enum string.

wildcard_patterns.name: not_eligible_application_out_of_scope
wildcard_patterns.description: OPT-IN (off by default, --include-optional): renames a protobuf ENUM VALUE name. Unproven - the eligibility gate is already cleared by protobuf_ineligible_bare, and rewriting an enum name risks a parse mismatch if the server sends the enum by name rather than by number. Left in the registry for experiments, not applied by default. Cross-platform: Rewrites NOT_ELIGIBLE_APPLICATION_OUT_OF_SCOPE enum string.

wildcard_patterns.name: eligibility_error_gate
wildcard_patterns.description: OPT-IN (off by default, --include-optional): machine-code gate, byte-exact per build. On agy 1.2.7 ineligibility_from_result_gate still matches but its companion eligibility_error_gate does NOT - the pair is broken, and rewriting a relative jump whose offset was derived from a different build risks landing mid-instruction in a 224 MB binary. The bare-literal rename alone is the proven fix, so these stay off unless a specific build has been verified end-to-end. MACHINE CODE (linux_x86_64 only): backend.(*AuthStatus).EligibilityError -> xor eax,eax; xor ebx,ebx; ret. Platform-specific Go binary patch, defense-in-depth alongside the protobuf rename.

wildcard_patterns.name: ineligibility_from_result_gate
wildcard_patterns.description: OPT-IN (off by default, --include-optional): machine-code gate, byte-exact per build. On agy 1.2.7 ineligibility_from_result_gate still matches but its companion eligibility_error_gate does NOT - the pair is broken, and rewriting a relative jump whose offset was derived from a different build risks landing mid-instruction in a 224 MB binary. The bare-literal rename alone is the proven fix, so these stay off unless a specific build has been verified end-to-end. MACHINE CODE (linux_x86_64 only): backend.IneligibilityFromResult -> jmp to eligible epilogue. Platform-specific Go binary patch, defense-in-depth.

wildcard_patterns.name: proxy_var_isolation
wildcard_patterns.description: OPT-IN (off by default, --include-optional): renames the lower-case 'https_proxy' env literal to same-length 'AG_LS_PROXY' so agy reads its proxy from a private variable instead of the ambient one. Deliberately leaves HTTPS_PROXY intact. Only enable when this tool supplies the proxy; otherwise it silently stops agy from honouring the user's own https_proxy.
